title: Simultaneous generic flattening of two proper families
statement: Let $S$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] which is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $f_i:X_i\to S$ for $i\in\{1,2\}$ be proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism]; either $X_i$ may be empty. There exist a nonempty quasi-compact open $U\subset S$ and a quasi-coherent ideal $I\subset\mathcal O_S$ of finite type with $I|_U=\mathcal O_U$. For the $U$-admissible blowup $v:T=\operatorname{Bl}_I S\to S$ [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], put $V=S\setminus V(I)$. For each $i$ the strict transform $X_i'\subset X_i\times_S T$ [def-nagata-strict-transform] is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented over $T$ (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated). It agrees with $X_i$ over $V$ and is the schematic closure of $(X_i)_V$ in $X_i\times_S T$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. The strict transform of $X_1\amalg X_2$ is the disjoint union $X_1'\amalg X_2'$.

source.place: Tag 081R, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up, applied to a finite disjoint union after Morphisms Tag 052A, proposition-generic-flatness; Divisors Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform. ILO Expose X, Theorem 3.4 proof Step 2, printed p.160.

proof.text: Form $W=X_1\amalg X_2$ and $g:W\to S$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Properness of $f_i$ includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For an affine open $A\subset S$, combine the two finite affine covers of $f_i^{-1}(A)$: they are affine opens of $g^{-1}(A)$ with the same finitely generated coordinate algebras. Thus $g$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This also works when either cover is empty.

source.place: Tags 01JB and 01JC, lemma-glue and lemma-glue-schemes, empty-overlap gluing; Morphisms Tag 01T0, finite type definition.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $W$ is Noetherian. Both $S$ and $W$ are locally Noetherian, hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. The Noetherian hypothesis includes quasi-compactness of $S$. Since $W$ is quasi-separated, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $g$ quasi-separated. These are precisely the base and morphism hypotheses needed for flattening.

source.place: Tag 01OV, definition-noetherian; Tag 01OY, lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated; Morphisms Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-generic-flat-finite-presentation] to $g$, whose finite type was proved in Step 1, over the integral $S$. Obtain a nonempty open $U$ on which $g$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], a descending chain of closed subsets has a minimal member among its terms and stabilizes there; hence the underlying space of $S$ is Noetherian. Then [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] makes every subset quasi-compact, in particular $U$ and, later, the centre complement $V$. Thus the required $U$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 052A, proposition-generic-flatness, structure-sheaf case; Properties Tag 01OZ, lemma-Noetherian-topology; Topology Tag 04ZA, lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flattening-by-admissible-blowup] to $(S,U,g)$. Steps 1--3 supply finite type and quasi-separatedness of $g$, a quasi-compact quasi-separated base, and a quasi-compact open with flat locally finitely presented restriction. It gives a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $I$, unit on $U$, and the $U$-admissible blowup $v:T\to S$, such that the strict transform $W'\subset W\times_ST$ is flat and of finite presentation over $T$. Write $V=S\setminus V(I)$; in particular $U\subset V$. The cited theorem identifies $W'$ with the schematic closure of $W_V$ in this fibre product.

The inverse images of the summands of $W=X_1\amalg X_2$ are disjoint clopen subschemes covering $W\times_ST$, so [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] identifies this fibre product with $(X_1\times_ST)\amalg(X_2\times_ST)$. Every $V\cap A$ for affine open $A\subset S$ is quasi-compact by Step 3; thus $V\to S$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its base change $j:(W\times_ST)_V\to W\times_ST$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Therefore [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] identifies its closure ideal with the kernel of $\mathcal O\to j_*\mathcal O$. Restricting this map to each clopen summand gives exactly $\mathcal O_{X_i\times_ST}\to(j_i)_*\mathcal O_{(X_i)_V}$, and kernels restrict componentwise. The closure is consequently $X_1'\amalg X_2'$, with each $X_i'$ the schematic closure of $(X_i)_V$, hence its strict transform by [def-nagata-strict-transform]. This is equality of ideal sheaves, including nilpotents.

source.place: Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform, applied on the two disjoint open-and-closed pieces; scheme-theoretic closure kernel definition.

proof.text: Each $X_i'$ is clopen in $W'$. Its local rings and affine open neighbourhoods are the same as in $W'$, so flatness and local finite presentation restrict by [def-weil-flat-morphism] and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For each affine $A\subset T$, the inverse image in $X_i'$ is closed in the quasi-compact inverse image in $W'$, hence quasi-compact. Moreover $\Delta_{X_i'/T}$ is the base change of $\Delta_{W'/T}$ along $X_i'\times_T X_i'\to W'\times_T W'$; thus it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). By [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], $X_i'\to T$ is quasi-separated. It is consequently of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 081R, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up, finite-presentation conclusion; Morphisms Tag 01TP, definition-finite-presentation; Schemes, quasi-compact diagonal definition.

proof.text: The same ideal is unit on $V$, which is quasi-compact by Step 3. Applying [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open] to $V$ gives $T\times_SV\cong V$. On this open, the kernel defining each closure in Step 5 is the kernel of an identity restriction, hence zero by [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Thus $X_i'$ agrees with $X_i$ over $V$. The closure identity and coproduct identity are those already proved in Step 5, so every conclusion follows. Empty summands remain empty throughout the kernel construction.
